summary.intent: Respond to PR #1154 review feedback by applying technically correct suggestions from Copilot and making the auth store constructor behavior consistent.
summary.outcome: Three files were patched (auth store, auth store test, TUI sink test), tests and lint passed, and the changes were committed as 'Address test store review feedback' and pushed to the PR branch.

repo: Integration tests run in 3 CI shards (a, b, c), which changes timing/scheduling enough to suppress locally-reproducible races.
The race condition in cmd/entire/cli/review was latent and schedule-sensitive — green CI does not rule out a real race.
Auth store files should enforce 0600 permissions; existing tests were missing a regression for broad-permission tightening.
PR #1154 is in the entireio/cli repo.

code.finding: File-backed auth constructor was not consistently enforcing 0600 permissions on existing store files; fixed to match expected behavior.
Added regression test for existing files with overly broad permissions being tightened to 0600 on open/use.
A test comment was stale (referenced old Bubble Tea behavior); updated to describe what the test actually does now.

workflow: Once a race detector fires in a Go package, all other tests in that package run may also be marked failed, even if they didn't trigger the race.
Copilot inline PR comments can be low-priority but technically correct; worth applying if the fix is small.
Stage only intended files explicitly (git add per-file) rather than staging everything, to avoid committing unrelated local changes.

friction: The Bubble Tea race (cancelreader Fd() called after close) was only reproducible locally due to TTY inheritance and scheduling — CI sharding masked it, making diagnosis harder.
TestEnableDefaultStrategy could hang locally because it inherited a TTY and entered an interactive prompt; CI suppresses this via the CI env var.
open_items: The underlying Bubble Tea race in cmd/entire/cli/review is a latent bug that CI hasn't caught — it should be properly fixed rather than relying on CI scheduling to avoid it.
The 'suppressed low-confidence' constructor note from Copilot was applied opportunistically; worth verifying the full constructor consistency across the auth package.
